b2.title: Northeasterly Winds Send Temperatures Tumbling
b2.zh: 東北季風來襲，氣溫急降

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Northeasterly winds to send mercury down to 11°C later this week

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Taiwan got its first real taste of winter this week. The Central Weather Administration warned that a strong northeasterly monsoon would sweep across the island from Wednesday, causing temperatures to drop sharply until at least Friday.

The change was most noticeable in northern Taiwan and Yilan. Daytime highs, which had been a comfortable 25 to 27 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, were expected to fall to just 18 to 20 degrees on Thursday. In some low-lying areas, overnight lows could dip to around 11 degrees.

Despite the chill, forecasters said most of the island would remain largely dry. Even so, a sudden swing in temperature can catch people off guard. It is a good idea to dress in layers and keep an eye on elderly relatives, who feel the cold more easily.

monsoon.def: a seasonal wind that brings a change in weather
monsoon.ex: The winter monsoon brings cold air.
monsoon.g: a northeasterly monsoon 東北季風。

sweep.def: to move quickly over a large area
sweep.ex: A storm swept across the city.
sweep.g: sweep across + 地方；過去式 swept。

noticeable.ex: There was a noticeable change in her voice.

low-lying.def: (of land) not much higher than the sea or the land around it
low-lying.g: 複合形容詞，放在名詞前：low-lying areas。

dip.def: to go down to a lower level for a short time

despite.ex: Despite the rain, we went out.
despite.g: Despite + 名詞（不可接子句）；= in spite of。

forecaster.def: a person who says what the weather will be like

layer.def: one piece of clothing worn over another
layer.g: dress in layers 洋蔥式穿法。

grammar.zh: V-ing 放句尾，說明前面動作造成的結果。
grammar.ex: causing temperatures to drop sharply

grammar.pt: 非限定關係子句 + 過去完成
grammar.zh: which had been… 補充說明「在那之前」的情況。
grammar.ex: Daytime highs, which had been a comfortable 25 to 27 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, were expected to fall

grammar.zh: 儘管…；後面接名詞，不接完整句子。
grammar.ex: Despite the chill, forecasters said most of the island would remain largely dry.

questions.q: Which areas felt the change the most?
What did forecasters say about rain?
opts: Most of the island would stay dry

questions.q: Why does the writer mention elderly relatives?
opts: They feel the cold more easily

keySentences.s: The change was most noticeable in northern Taiwan and Yilan.
In some low-lying areas, overnight lows could dip to around 11 degrees.

b2.title: Rare Treasures Draw Crowds to Taipei's Stamp Exhibition
b2.zh: 珍稀郵票吸引人潮到台北

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Rare Stamps Take Center Stage as Taipei World Stamp Exhibition Opens November 20

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Stamp lovers from around the world are gathering in Taipei this week for a major international exhibition. The event opened at the Taipei World Trade Center on November 20 and runs until November 25, with free admission for all visitors.

Among the highlights is the famous "Inverted Jenny", a 1918 American stamp on which the airplane was accidentally printed upside down. Only a small number of these error stamps ever reached the public, which is why collectors have treasured them for over a century.

The exhibition also marks the 130th anniversary of Chunghwa Post, and its organizers have chosen innovation and sustainability as the main theme. Interest was clearly high even before the doors opened: a set of new Pokémon stamps proved so popular that most of them had already sold out.

gather.def: to come together in one place
gather.g: are gathering 正在聚集；不及物動詞。

admission.def: the right to enter a place, or the money you pay for it

highlight.def: the best or most exciting part of something
highlight.ex: The highlight of the trip was the beach.
highlight.g: Among the highlights is… 倒裝句：精彩之一是…。

treasure.def: to keep something carefully because it is valuable
treasure.g: have treasured 現在完成式，表示一直以來。

anniversary.def: the day on which an important event happened in a past year

sustainability.def: using resources in a way that can continue without harming the earth

prove.def: to be found to be something

grammar.zh: on which = on the stamp；關係子句前帶介系詞。
grammar.ex: a 1918 American stamp on which the airplane was accidentally printed upside down

grammar.zh: 用 which 指前面整句，表示「這就是為什麼…」。
grammar.ex: which is why collectors have treasured them for over a century

grammar.pt: 過去完成 had already + p.p.
grammar.zh: 比過去某時間更早發生的事。
grammar.ex: a set of new Pokémon stamps proved so popular that most of them had already sold out

Why is the Inverted Jenny so valuable?
opts: It has a famous printing error
It is the oldest stamp in the world

questions.q: What shows that the Pokémon stamps were popular?
opts: Most sold out before the show opened
They were given away for free

keySentences.s: Stamp lovers from around the world are gathering in Taipei this week for a major international exhibition.
The event opened at the Taipei World Trade Center on November 20 and runs until November 25, with free admission for all visitors.

b2.title: Regular Park Visits Linked to Better Mental Health
b2.zh: 常去公園，孩子心理更健康

source.name: University of Bristol：Going to the park at least once a week can improve children's mental health

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Taking children to the park every week may do more than burn off energy. A new study from the University of Bristol suggests that regular visits to parks and playgrounds are linked to better mental health as children grow up.

The researchers analyzed data on more than 4,000 children taking part in Children of the 90s, a long-term study that has followed families since the early 1990s. Children who were taken to a park at least once a week from birth to the age of 11 scored around 16.5 percent higher on measures of mental well-being.

According to the team, parks offer something that homes and classrooms often cannot: open space for active, imaginative play. This kind of play helps children build confidence. The researchers are now calling on city planners to make sure safe, accessible parks are available to every family.

burn off.def: to use up energy or calories through activity
burn off.ex: Kids need to burn off energy after school.
burn off.g: burn off energy 放電、消耗體力。

link.def: to show that two things are connected
link.g: be linked to + 名詞：和…有關。

analyze.def: to study something carefully to understand it

measure.def: a way of judging or testing something
measure.ex: Test scores are one measure of success.
measure.g: measures of… …的衡量指標；也可當動詞。

well-being.def: the state of feeling healthy and happy
well-being.g: 不可數名詞；mental well-being 心理健康。

accessible.def: easy to reach, enter or use
accessible.ex: The park is accessible by bus.

grammar.zh: 和…有關（被動）。
grammar.ex: regular visits to parks and playgrounds are linked to better mental health

grammar.zh: 孩子是「被帶去」公園。
grammar.ex: Children who were taken to a park at least once a week

grammar.zh: 呼籲某人做某事。
grammar.ex: The researchers are now calling on city planners to make sure safe, accessible parks are available to every family.

questions.q: Who carried out the study?
opts: Researchers at the University of Bristol

questions.q: How much higher did weekly park visitors score?
What do the researchers want city planners to do?
opts: Provide safe parks for every family

keySentences.s: Taking children to the park every week may do more than burn off energy.
The researchers are now calling on city planners to make sure safe, accessible parks are available to every family.

b2.title: How to Make Stress Your Friend

source.name: TED：Kelly McGonigal, How to make stress your friend

b2.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Most of us have been told that stress is bad for our health. In one of the most watched TED talks of all time, health psychologist Kelly McGonigal admits that she used to deliver the same warning, until new research changed her mind.

She describes a study that followed about 30,000 adults in the United States for eight years. People who experienced a lot of stress had a higher risk of dying, but only if they also believed that stress was harmful. Those who felt stressed but did not see it as a threat were among the least likely to die.

McGonigal's message is that our mindset matters. When we view a racing heart as the body preparing us to rise to a challenge, our blood vessels can stay more relaxed. She also points out that stress encourages us to reach out to others, and that connecting with people builds resilience.

admit.def: to agree that something is true, often unwillingly
admit.ex: He admitted that he was wrong.

experience.def: to have something happen to you
experience.ex: Many people experience stress at work.
experience.g: 當動詞時後面直接接受詞。

risk.def: the chance that something bad will happen
risk.ex: a high risk of heart disease
risk.g: a higher risk of + V-ing／名詞。

threat.ex: Pollution is a threat to wildlife.
threat.g: see it as a threat 把它看成威脅。

mindset.def: a person's way of thinking about things
mindset.g: Our mindset matters. 心態很重要。

rise to.def: to deal well with a difficult situation
rise to.g: rise to a challenge 迎接挑戰。

resilience.def: the ability to recover quickly from difficulty
resilience.g: 不可數名詞；形容詞 resilient。

grammar.zh: 過去常常…（現在不再）。
grammar.ex: she used to deliver the same warning

grammar.zh: 只有在…的情況下。
grammar.ex: but only if they also believed that stress was harmful

grammar.zh: 把 A 看作 B。
grammar.ex: When we view a racing heart as the body preparing us to rise to a challenge

questions.q: How long did the study follow people?
Which group had a higher risk of dying?
opts: Stressed people who believed stress was harmful
People with no stress at all

questions.q: What does stress encourage us to do, according to McGonigal?

keySentences.s: McGonigal's message is that our mindset matters.
Those who felt stressed but did not see it as a threat were among the least likely to die.

c1.title: A Northeasterly Surge Brings Taiwan's First Real Chill
c1.zh: 東北季風增強，台灣迎來第一波寒意

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Northeasterly winds to send mercury down to 11°C later this week

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: With daytime highs still in the mid-twenties early in the week, many people in Taiwan were caught off guard by the arrival of winter. The Central Weather Administration forecast that a vigorous northeasterly monsoon would push down from the north on Wednesday, triggering a pronounced drop in temperatures that was set to last until at least Friday.

Nowhere was the shift more apparent than in northern Taiwan and Yilan. Daytime highs that had hovered around a pleasant 25 to 27 degrees Celsius on Wednesday were projected to slump to between 18 and 20 degrees by Thursday, while low-lying areas could see overnight readings of roughly 11 degrees.

There was, however, a silver lining. Forecasters expected the bulk of the island to stay dry, sparing commuters the damp, bone-chilling combination of rain and wind that often accompanies such cold snaps.

Sudden temperature swings of this magnitude are more than a minor inconvenience. Rapid cooling forces the body to work harder to keep warm, which is why doctors routinely urge older people and those with heart conditions to wrap up well and avoid abrupt transitions from heated rooms to the cold outdoors.

vigorous.def: strong, active and full of energy

pronounced.g: a pronounced drop 明顯下降；注意不是 pronounce 的「發音」。

apparent.ex: It was apparent that she was tired.
apparent.g: more apparent than… 比…更明顯。

hover.def: to stay at or near a particular level

slump.def: to fall suddenly by a large amount

silver lining.def: something good in a bad situation
silver lining.ex: Every cloud has a silver lining.
silver lining.g: 慣用語，常說 There is a silver lining。

spare.def: to save someone from something unpleasant
spare.ex: She was spared the long wait.
spare.g: spare + 人 + 事：讓某人免受…。

magnitude.def: the large size or importance of something
magnitude.g: of this magnitude 這麼大規模的。

grammar.pt: 否定副詞倒裝 Nowhere was…
grammar.zh: Nowhere 放句首，主詞和 be 動詞倒裝，加強語氣。
grammar.ex: Nowhere was the shift more apparent than in northern Taiwan and Yilan.

grammar.zh: V-ing 補充說明前句帶來的結果。
grammar.ex: sparing commuters the damp, bone-chilling combination of rain and wind

grammar.zh: 指前面整件事，引出結果或理由。
grammar.ex: which is why doctors routinely urge older people and those with heart conditions to wrap up well

questions.q: What can be inferred about the weather early in the week?
opts: It had already been very cold

questions.q: Why does the writer call the dry weather a "silver lining"?
opts: It spared people the worse mix of cold and rain

questions.q: According to the last paragraph, why are sudden cold spells a concern?
opts: They make the body work harder to stay warm

keySentences.s: There was, however, a silver lining.
Nowhere was the shift more apparent than in northern Taiwan and Yilan.

c1.title: Errors, Anniversaries and Pokémon: Inside Taipei's Stamp Show
c1.zh: 錯版、週年與寶可夢：走進台北世界郵展

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Rare Stamps Take Center Stage as Taipei World Stamp Exhibition Opens November 20

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: For six days in late November, the Taipei World Trade Center has been transformed into a magnet for philatelists. The international stamp exhibition, which opened on November 20 and closes on November 25, is free to enter, a decision that lowers the barrier for casual visitors who might never otherwise set foot in a stamp show.

Pride of place goes to the "Inverted Jenny", arguably the most celebrated mistake in the history of printing. Issued in the United States in 1918, the stamp shows a biplane flying upside down, the result of a sheet being fed into the press the wrong way round. Precisely because so few copies escaped into circulation, the error has become a prized collectible.

The exhibition doubles as a celebration of Chunghwa Post's 130th anniversary, and its organizers have framed the event around innovation and sustainability. These themes may seem at odds with a hobby so closely tied to paper and tradition.

If anyone doubted whether stamps still resonate with younger generations, a new series of Pokémon designs settled the question: demand was so intense that most of the stamps had sold out before the exhibition even began.

magnet.def: a place or thing that attracts many people
magnet.ex: The city is a magnet for tourists.

philatelist.def: a person who collects and studies stamps

barrier.def: something that prevents people from doing something
barrier.ex: Cost is a barrier to education.
barrier.g: lower the barrier 降低門檻。

pride of place.def: the most important or noticeable position
pride of place.ex: The trophy has pride of place on the shelf.
pride of place.g: Pride of place goes to… 最受矚目的是…。

arguably.def: used to say that something can be considered true
arguably.ex: She is arguably the best player.
arguably.g: 放在最高級前，語氣保留但肯定。

circulation.def: the movement of money, stamps or papers among the public
circulation.g: escape into circulation 流入市面。

at odds.ex: His words are at odds with his actions.
at odds.g: be at odds with… 與…不一致。

resonate.def: to have special meaning or importance for someone
resonate.ex: The film resonated with young viewers.

grammar.zh: precisely 強調「正是因為」。
grammar.ex: Precisely because so few copies escaped into circulation, the error has become a prized collectible.

grammar.zh: 同時兼作…。
grammar.ex: The exhibition doubles as a celebration of Chunghwa Post's 130th anniversary

grammar.zh: 如此…以致於…。
grammar.ex: demand was so intense that most of the stamps had sold out before the exhibition even began

opts: It makes it easier for casual visitors to come
It raises money for the post office
It limits the size of the crowd

questions.q: What caused the Inverted Jenny error?
opts: A sheet was fed into the press the wrong way
The designer drew the plane upside down

opts: Stamps are closely tied to paper and tradition

keySentences.s: These themes may seem at odds with a hobby so closely tied to paper and tradition.

c1.title: Why a Weekly Trip to the Park Could Shape a Child's Mind
c1.zh: 每週一次公園行，如何影響孩子的心理

source.name: University of Bristol：Going to the park at least once a week can improve children's mental health

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Parents who drag their children to the local park on a drizzly Saturday may be doing more good than they realize. Research from the University of Bristol indicates that habitual visits to parks and playgrounds throughout childhood are associated with measurably better mental health.

The findings draw on Children of the 90s, one of the most extensive long-running studies of its kind, which has tracked thousands of families since the early 1990s. Among the more than 4,000 children examined, those taken to a park at least weekly from birth until the age of 11 scored roughly 16.5 percent higher on assessments of mental health than their peers.

Crucially, the study points to an association rather than proof of cause and effect, since families who visit parks often may differ in other ways too. Nonetheless, the pattern fits what is known about unstructured outdoor play, which gives children room to take small risks, exercise their imagination and develop a sense of competence.

The conclusion has a clear policy dimension. If green space genuinely nurtures well-being, then ensuring that every neighborhood has a safe, welcoming park is not a luxury but a matter of public health and fairness.

draw on.def: to use information or experience as a source

peer.def: a person of the same age or group
peer.ex: She was popular with her peers.
peer.g: than their peers 比同齡孩子。

association.ex: an association between diet and health

nonetheless.def: despite what has just been said
nonetheless.ex: It was hard; nonetheless, we finished.

unstructured.def: without a fixed plan or organization

competence.def: the ability to do something well

nurture.def: to help something develop and grow

grammar.zh: 而不是…（對比兩個名詞）。
grammar.ex: the study points to an association rather than proof of cause and effect

grammar.zh: 不是 A 而是 B。
grammar.ex: is not a luxury but a matter of public health and fairness

grammar.zh: 條件句，then 強調結論。
grammar.ex: If green space genuinely nurtures well-being, then ensuring that every neighborhood has a safe, welcoming park is not a luxury

questions.q: What does the writer stress about the study's findings?
opts: They show a link, not proof of cause
They prove parks cause better health

questions.q: Which detail describes the Children of the 90s study?
opts: It has followed families for decades

questions.q: What does the final paragraph argue?
opts: Safe parks are a public health issue

keySentences.s: Crucially, the study points to an association rather than proof of cause and effect, since families who visit parks often may differ in other ways too.
The findings draw on Children of the 90s, one of the most extensive long-running studies of its kind, which has tracked thousands of families since the early 1990s.

c1.title: Rethinking Stress: Kelly McGonigal's Surprising Case
c1.zh: 重新思考壓力：凱莉・麥高尼格的反直覺觀點

source.name: TED：Kelly McGonigal, How to make stress your friend

c1.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Few health messages are repeated as relentlessly as the claim that stress makes us ill. In her widely viewed TED talk, health psychologist Kelly McGonigal confesses that she spent years reinforcing that very message, only to be confronted by evidence that complicated it.

The turning point was a study that tracked roughly 30,000 American adults over eight years. High levels of stress were associated with a 43 percent greater risk of dying, yet this held true only for participants who also believed that stress was damaging to their health. Those who reported plenty of stress but did not regard it as harmful had some of the lowest mortality rates in the study.

From this, McGonigal draws a provocative conclusion: how we interpret our physical reactions may shape their consequences. A pounding heart and quickened breath can be reframed as signs that the body is mobilizing energy to meet a challenge, and people who learned to see stress this way showed a healthier response, with blood vessels that stayed relaxed.

She also highlights a less familiar side of the stress response: the release of oxytocin, a hormone that nudges us to seek and offer support. Seen in this light, stress is not merely something to be eliminated. Handled well, it can be a catalyst for courage and connection.

relentlessly.def: without stopping or becoming less strong

reinforce.def: to make an idea or feeling stronger
reinforce.g: reinforcing 動名詞，接在 spend years 後。

confront.def: to make someone face something difficult
confront.ex: She was confronted with the truth.
confront.g: be confronted by/with… 被迫面對…。

mortality.def: the number of deaths in a group
mortality.g: mortality rates 死亡率（常用複數）。

provocative.zh: 發人深省的、引起爭議的

reframe.def: to think about something in a different way
reframe.ex: Try to reframe failure as learning.
reframe.g: be reframed as… 被重新詮釋為…。

mobilize.def: to bring together resources for a purpose
mobilize.ex: The body mobilizes energy under stress.

catalyst.def: something that causes an important change
catalyst.ex: The crisis was a catalyst for reform.

grammar.zh: 結果卻…（出乎意料的轉折）。
grammar.ex: only to be confronted by evidence that complicated it

grammar.zh: 對…成立、適用。
grammar.ex: this held true only for participants who also believed that stress was damaging to their health

grammar.zh: 省略主詞的被動分詞構句，表示條件。
grammar.ex: Seen in this light, stress is not merely something to be eliminated.

questions.q: What happened to McGonigal's earlier view of stress?
opts: New evidence made her rethink it
She proved it was completely right

questions.q: According to the study, who faced the higher risk of death?
opts: Stressed people who saw stress as harmful

questions.q: What role does oxytocin play, as described in the talk?
opts: It nudges people to seek and give support
It makes the heart beat faster

keySentences.s: Handled well, it can be a catalyst for courage and connection.
Few health messages are repeated as relentlessly as the claim that stress makes us ill.

b2.title: Voyager 1 Crosses the One Light-Day Line
b2.zh: 航海家1號跨越一光日里程碑

source.name: ScienceDaily：NASA's Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Nearly half a century after leaving Earth, NASA's Voyager 1 has become the first spacecraft ever to sit one full light-day away from home. The milestone, which engineers confirmed by tracking the probe's radio signal, was reached on November 18, when the craft was roughly 25.9 billion kilometers from our planet.
This enormous distance creates practical challenges. Any command sent from Earth now needs 24 hours to arrive, and the team must wait another day before learning whether it worked.

Keeping the aging probe alive has become a careful balancing act. Its power supply drops by about four watts every year, so engineers have switched off several systems to save energy. Their latest measures should keep the current instruments running until at least the summer of 2027.
However, the celebration comes with some worry: no data has reached NASA since November 14, and engineers are still investigating the cause.

milestone.def: a very important event in the development of something
milestone.ex: Graduating was a big milestone in her life.
milestone.g: The milestone, which…：milestone 後接補充說明的關係子句。

confirm.def: to say or show that something is true
confirm.g: confirmed by tracking…：by + V-ing 表示用什麼方法。

enormous.ex: They live in an enormous house.
enormous.g: This enormous distance：比 big 更強烈的形容詞。

practical.def: relating to real situations rather than ideas
practical.g: practical challenges：實際操作上的困難。

command.def: an order given to a person or machine
command.g: Any command sent from Earth：sent 是過去分詞，省略 that is。

aging.ex: The city has an aging population.
aging.g: the aging probe：現在分詞當形容詞，表示正在變老。

instrument.def: a tool used for scientific measurement
instrument.ex: The ship carries instruments to measure the wind.
instrument.g: keep the current instruments running：keep + 受詞 + V-ing。

investigate.def: to try to find out the facts about something
investigate.g: are still investigating：現在進行式表示仍在進行中。

grammar.zh: 用逗號隔開，補充說明前面的名詞
grammar.ex: The milestone, which engineers confirmed by tracking the probe's radio signal, was reached on November 18

grammar.zh: V-ing 片語當主詞，動詞用單數
grammar.ex: Keeping the aging probe alive has become a careful balancing act

grammar.zh: 前面說原因，so 帶出採取的行動
grammar.ex: so engineers have switched off several systems to save energy

grammar.zh: 使某物持續保持某狀態
grammar.ex: keep the current instruments running

questions.q: How did engineers confirm the milestone?
opts: By taking photos of the probe
By tracking the probe's radio signal

questions.q: Why must the team wait two days to know whether a command worked?
opts: The probe only works every other day.
Engineers check data twice a week.

questions.q: What is the main worry mentioned at the end?
opts: No data has reached NASA since November 14.
The probe is moving toward Earth.

keySentences.s: This enormous distance creates practical challenges.
Keeping the aging probe alive has become a careful balancing act.

b2.title: How Often You Move May Matter Most
b2.zh: 運動頻率可能比強度更重要

source.name: ScienceDaily：For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: If you have been skipping workouts because you think only intense exercise counts, a new Norwegian study offers some encouraging news. Researchers followed 10,460 university students aged 18 to 35, asking about how often, how hard and how long they exercised.

A year later, the students completed a mental health assessment. Those who were less active were more likely to meet the criteria for anxiety or depression, and frequency turned out to be the most consistent factor.

Interestingly, the patterns differed between men and women. Among women, lower intensity was linked to more symptoms, while for men the total number of weekly hours mattered more. The risk kept falling as weekly exercise increased, up to about ten hours.
Because the study was observational, it cannot show cause and effect. Still, the authors note that their results fit the WHO's advice of 150 minutes of activity a week.

symptom.ex: A cough is a common symptom of a cold.
symptom.g: was linked to more symptoms：be linked to 表示「與…有關」。

observational.def: based on watching and recording, not on experiments
observational.ex: An observational study cannot prove cause.
observational.g: Because the study was observational：說明研究限制。

b2.title: Taiwanese Tech Firms Pitch Smart City Ideas in Bangkok
b2.zh: 台灣科技業者在曼谷推銷智慧城市方案

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Taiwanese tech firms showcase smart city solutions at Thailand expo

b2.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 B2 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Taiwanese companies took a wide range of smart city technology to Bangkok this month, hoping to win customers at Smart City Expo Thailand 2026. The three-day event, which opened on November 18, featured products covering healthcare, transportation, energy management and artificial intelligence.

For the Taipei City government, which brought a delegation of 12 firms, it was the first appearance at the expo. Meanwhile, a Taiwan AI Solution Pavilion organized by the Taipei Computer Association showcased 10 local AI companies working on edge computing and smart energy.

One eye-catching product was a display that remains readable in bright sunlight and can hold an image without a constant power supply. Another firm said its data storage systems were already being used in parts of Thailand.
According to the report, Thai agencies and businesses showed particular interest in solutions for transport and public safety.

b2.title: The Brain-Changing Benefits of Exercise

source.name: TED：Wendy Suzuki, The brain-changing benefits of exercise

b2.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Neuroscientist Wendy Suzuki opens her TED talk with a personal story. Years ago, she was so focused on her research at New York University that she had almost no social life and felt out of shape. When she finally started going to exercise classes, she noticed that her mood and her memory both improved.
That discovery led her to change the direction of her lab and study what exercise does to the brain.

According to Suzuki, a single workout releases chemicals such as dopamine and serotonin that can lift your mood immediately, and it may sharpen your attention for a couple of hours afterward. Over the long term, regular exercise can help the brain grow new cells in the hippocampus, an area crucial for memory.

She argues this may make the brain more resistant to diseases like dementia. Her recommendation is practical: three to four sessions a week of about 30 minutes, including activity that raises your heart rate.

personal.ex: He told us a personal story.
personal.g: a personal story：演講常用的開場方式。

out of shape.ex: I'm out of shape after the holidays.
out of shape.g: felt out of shape：feel + 形容詞片語。

notice.ex: Did you notice the new sign?
notice.g: noticed that…：notice 後接 that 子句。

direction.g: change the direction of her lab：改變研究方向。

release.def: to let a substance flow out
release.g: a single workout releases chemicals：主詞單數，動詞加 s。

immediately.g: lift your mood immediately：副詞放在句尾修飾動詞。

crucial.g: an area crucial for memory：形容詞片語後置修飾 area。

resistant.ex: This plant is resistant to disease.
resistant.g: more resistant to diseases：resistant to + 名詞。

grammar.zh: 如此…以致於…

grammar.zh: 促使某人做某事
grammar.ex: That discovery led her to change the direction of her lab

grammar.zh: 逗號後的名詞片語補充說明前面的名詞
grammar.ex: the hippocampus, an area crucial for memory

questions.q: What made Suzuki change her research?
Where can regular exercise help the brain grow new cells?
What does she recommend?
opts: Three to four sessions a week of about 30 minutes

keySentences.s: Neuroscientist Wendy Suzuki opens her TED talk with a personal story.
She argues this may make the brain more resistant to diseases like dementia.

c1.title: A Day Away: Voyager 1's Lonely Milestone
c1.zh: 一光日之遙：航海家1號的孤獨里程碑

source.name: ScienceDaily：NASA's Voyager 1 is now so far away that light takes 24 hours to reach it

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Launched in 1977 and still drifting outward at roughly 61,000 kilometers per hour, Voyager 1 crossed a threshold on November 18 that no human-made object had crossed before: it now lies a full light-day from Earth. At about 25.9 billion kilometers, the distance is so vast that even a radio signal, traveling at the speed of light, needs an entire day to bridge it.

For the engineers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the milestone is as much a logistical headache as a cause for celebration. Every instruction now takes 24 hours to arrive, meaning that a simple exchange of command and confirmation stretches over two days.

Not only is the distance growing, but the probe's power is steadily dwindling, falling by around four watts a year. Having already switched off a number of systems in earlier rounds of conservation, the team expects its latest measures to keep the current instruments working until at least summer 2027.

Even so, the mood is far from triumphant. Since November 14, no science or engineering data has come back from the spacecraft, and engineers are still trying to pin down why. Given the probe's age and its history of clogged thrusters and computer glitches, few would be shocked by another setback, yet the team has coaxed Voyager back from the brink before.

threshold.def: the level or point at which something starts or changes
threshold.ex: The temperature passed a critical threshold.
threshold.g: crossed a threshold that…：that 子句說明是怎樣的門檻。

vast.def: extremely big in size or amount
vast.ex: The desert is vast and empty.
vast.g: so vast that…：so + 形容詞 + that 表結果。

logistical.def: relating to the practical organization of a complex task
logistical.ex: Moving 500 people is a logistical challenge.
logistical.g: a logistical headache：headache 比喻棘手的問題。

dwindle.def: to become gradually smaller or fewer
dwindle.ex: Their savings dwindled over the years.
dwindle.g: is steadily dwindling：進行式強調持續減少中。

conservation.def: the careful use of something so that it is not wasted
conservation.g: rounds of conservation：一輪輪的節能措施。

pin down.def: to discover the exact facts about something
pin down.ex: Doctors couldn't pin down the cause.
pin down.g: trying to pin down why：後接疑問詞 why。

setback.ex: The injury was a setback for the team.

brink.def: the point where something bad is about to happen
brink.ex: The company was on the brink of failure.
brink.g: back from the brink：從危急邊緣救回，常見慣用語。

grammar.pt: 分詞構句（過去分詞＋現在分詞）
grammar.zh: 以分詞片語開頭描述主詞
grammar.ex: Launched in 1977 and still drifting outward

grammar.zh: 既是 A 也是 B，兩者程度相當

grammar.zh: Not only 放句首，助動詞移到主詞前
grammar.ex: Not only is the distance growing

grammar.zh: Having + p.p. 表示先發生的動作

keySentences.s: Not only is the distance growing, but the probe's power is steadily dwindling, falling by around four watts a year.

c1.title: Little and Often: Rethinking Exercise for the Mind
c1.zh: 少量多次：重新思考運動與心理健康

source.name: ScienceDaily：For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: For anyone who equates a worthwhile workout with gasping for breath, a study from Western Norway University of Applied Sciences may come as a relief. Tracking 10,460 full-time students across Norway, the researchers recorded how often, how intensely and for how long each one exercised, then revisited them a year later with a diagnostic questionnaire.

The picture that emerged was fairly clear-cut. Students who were less active were more prone to anxiety and depression twelve months on, and of all the measures, frequency proved the most reliable predictor, outweighing both intensity and duration.

Beneath that headline, however, lay some intriguing differences. Women who exercised at lower intensity reported more symptoms, whereas men appeared to be more affected by how many hours they logged each week. In both groups, the risk continued to fall as weekly activity climbed toward roughly ten hours.

The authors are careful not to overstate their case: the study is observational, so it cannot establish that exercise directly protects mental health. Nonetheless, their findings sit comfortably alongside the WHO's recommendation of 150 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity a week, suggesting that showing up regularly may count for more than pushing hard.

equate.def: to consider one thing to be the same as another
equate.ex: Many people equate money with success.
equate.g: equate A with B：把 A 等同於 B。

relief.def: a feeling of happiness that something bad is not true
relief.ex: It was a relief to hear the news.
relief.g: come as a relief：對某人來說是一種寬慰。

prone.g: more prone to anxiety：prone to + 名詞。

outweigh.def: to be greater or more important than something
outweigh.g: outweighing both…：分詞構句補充結果。

log.def: to record an amount, such as time or distance
log.g: how many hours they logged：logged 表示累計的運動時數。

overstate.def: to say something is more important than it really is
overstate.g: careful not to overstate：不定詞否定把 not 放在 to 前。

grammar.zh: 介系詞片語放句首，主詞動詞倒裝
grammar.ex: Beneath that headline, however, lay some intriguing differences

grammar.zh: V-ing 片語交代背景動作
grammar.ex: Tracking 10,460 full-time students across Norway

grammar.zh: be careful not to V
grammar.ex: The authors are careful not to overstate their case

grammar.pt: 慣用語 come as a relief
grammar.zh: 使人鬆一口氣
grammar.ex: may come as a relief

questions.q: Who would most likely find this study a relief?
opts: People who already train ten hours a week
People who think exercise only counts if it is exhausting

questions.q: What does "showing up regularly may count for more than pushing hard" imply?
opts: Consistency matters more than effort level.

opts: They found no link at all.

c1.title: Taiwan Bets on Smart City Know-How in Southeast Asia
c1.zh: 台灣以智慧城市技術進軍東南亞

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Taiwanese tech firms showcase smart city solutions at Thailand expo

c1.note: 學習用短文，依參考資料改寫成 C1 程度，延伸閱讀請看來源連結。
paras: Eager to turn their engineering strengths into overseas sales, Taiwanese technology firms descended on Bangkok last week for Smart City Expo Thailand 2026. Over three days from November 18, they pitched everything from healthcare and transport systems to energy-management tools and artificial intelligence, hoping to win new customers and partners abroad.

The Taipei City government, making its debut at the event, arrived with a dozen companies in tow. Alongside them, the Taipei Computer Association ran a Taiwan AI Solution Pavilion, where ten domestic firms demonstrated edge computing, AI processing and smart-energy technology to visitors throughout the event.

Among the more unusual exhibits was a cholesteric liquid crystal display, which stays legible under harsh sunlight and retains its image without drawing continuous power. Elsewhere, a data-storage company noted that its equipment was already handling round-the-clock video in Pattaya and southern Thailand.

Judging by the reception, the trip may pay off. Thai government agencies and private companies reportedly showed keen interest, particularly in transport, security and safety, suggesting that Taiwan's smart city know-how could find a ready market in the region. For a city taking part for the very first time, that would be an encouraging start.

eager.def: wanting very much to do something
eager.ex: She was eager to start her new job.
eager.g: Eager to V 放句首，形容詞片語修飾後面的主詞 firms。

descend.def: descend on: to arrive at a place in large numbers
descend.g: descended on Bangkok：descend on + 地點，表示大批人到來。

debut.def: the first time someone appears in public
debut.ex: The singer made her debut at 18.
debut.g: making its debut：make one's debut 首次登場。

in tow.ex: She arrived with her kids in tow.
in tow.g: with a dozen companies in tow：with + 受詞 + 片語。

legible.def: clear enough to be read easily
legible.g: stays legible：stay + 形容詞，表示保持某狀態。

retain.def: to keep or continue to have something
retain.g: retains its image：比 keep 更正式。

round-the-clock.def: happening all day and all night
round-the-clock.g: 複合形容詞放在名詞 video 前。

pay off.ex: All her hard work paid off.
pay off.g: the trip may pay off：may 表推測。

c1.title: Why Your Brain Wants You to Move
c1.zh: 大腦為什麼需要你動起來

source.name: TED：Wendy Suzuki, The brain-changing benefits of exercise

c1.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: By her own account, Wendy Suzuki's career was thriving while her personal life had stalled. A neuroscientist at New York University, she had poured so much into her lab that she had little social life and felt out of shape. It was only when she decided to take up regular exercise classes that she noticed something she, of all people, might have predicted: her mood lifted and her memory seemed sharper.

Rather than treat this as a happy coincidence, Suzuki redirected her research toward the effects of physical activity on the brain. In her TED talk, she lays out what she sees as both immediate and lasting benefits.

A single bout of exercise, she explains, floods the brain with neurotransmitters such as dopamine and serotonin, boosting mood and improving attention for up to a couple of hours. Repeated over months, however, exercise appears to stimulate the growth of new cells in the hippocampus, enlarging a structure vital to long-term memory.

Seen this way, a workout is less a chore than an investment, one that may help shield the brain against conditions such as Alzheimer's disease and dementia. Tellingly, her prescription is modest: three or four sessions a week, roughly half an hour each, with no gym membership required.

stall.g: had stalled 過去完成式，與 was thriving 形成對比。

take up.def: to start doing a new activity
take up.ex: He took up running last year.
take up.g: decided to take up…：decide to + 原形動詞片語。

coincidence.def: a surprising situation where things happen together by chance
coincidence.ex: What a coincidence to meet you here!
coincidence.g: Rather than treat this as a happy coincidence：treat A as B 把 A 當作 B。

redirect.def: to change the direction or purpose of something
redirect.ex: She redirected her energy into study.
redirect.g: redirected her research toward…：toward 表示新方向。

bout.def: a short period of an activity
bout.g: A single bout of exercise：與 repeated over months 對照。

stimulate.def: to make something grow or become more active
stimulate.g: appears to stimulate：appear to V 表示看起來會…。

shield.def: to protect someone or something from harm

prescription.def: advice about what someone should do (originally from a doctor)
prescription.g: her prescription is modest：借醫療用語比喻她的建議。

grammar.pt: 強調句 It was only when … that …
grammar.zh: 強調時間條件
grammar.ex: It was only when she decided to take up regular exercise classes that she noticed

grammar.zh: 與其…不如…
grammar.ex: Rather than treat this as a happy coincidence

grammar.zh: 與其說是 A，不如說是 B
grammar.ex: a workout is less a chore than an investment

grammar.pt: 獨立分詞構句 with + 受詞 + p.p.
grammar.zh: 附帶狀況
grammar.ex: with no gym membership required

questions.q: Why does the writer say "she, of all people, might have predicted" the change?
opts: She had studied exercise for years.
She is a brain scientist, so the effect fits her field.

questions.q: Calling a workout "an investment" implies that…
opts: its benefits build up over time
it costs a lot of money

questions.q: What does "her prescription is modest" suggest?
opts: She thinks exercise is not very useful.

keySentences.s: By her own account, Wendy Suzuki's career was thriving while her personal life had stalled.
Tellingly, her prescription is modest: three or four sessions a week, roughly half an hour each, with no gym membership required.
